questions.stem: All of the following are genetic susceptibility for type 1 diabetes except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Mutation in KCNJ11
  • KCNJ11 (Potassium Inwardly Rectifying Channel, Subfamily J, Member 11) is a gene associated with a rare form of diabetes called neonatal diabetes.
  • This gene is not typically associated with an increased risk of type 1 diabetes.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1107-09

questions.stem: The most common cause of death in diabetes is-
questions.solutionHtml:
Myocardial infarction
  • Myocardial infarction, caused by atherosclerosis of the coronary arteries, is the most common cause of death in diabetics.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1117

questions.stem: The most constant histological features of diabetes that can be seen in the skin, smooth muscle, retina, and kidney are?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thickening of basement membrane
  • The most constant histological feature of diabetes that can be seen in the skin, smooth muscle, retina, and kidney is the thickening of the basement membrane.
  • It is caused by the accumulation of certain substances, such as advanced glycation end products (AGEs) and extracellular matrix components, as a result of chronic hyperglycemia.
  • This thickening can impair the normal function of these tissues and contribute to the development of diabetic complications.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1118

questions.stem: All of the following histological features seen in diabetic nephropathy except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Cortical sclerosis
  • Cortical sclerosis, or interstitial fibrosis, is not a characteristic histological feature of diabetic nephropathy.
  • It refers to the replacement of normal kidney tissue with fibrous scar tissue in the cortical region.
  • While chronic kidney disease can lead to cortical sclerosis, it is not specific to diabetic nephropathy.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1118

questions.stemHtml: A 47-year-old patient is on irregular medication of oral hypoglycemic drugs, and at present has a random blood sugar of 200 mg/dl. At present he has oliguria. A renal biopsy was performed and the histopathological diagram is shown below. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Diabetic glomerulopathy
  • The given clinical scenario of irregular medication of oral hypoglycemic drugs, elevated random blood sugar levels, and the histopathological finding of nodular sclerosis with oliguria suggest the diagnosis of diabetic glomerulopathy.
  • The presence of nodular sclerosis, or Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules, is a hallmark feature of diabetic glomerulopathy.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1118
